settings.llmskills_cinematic_translation_desc: Rewrites each translated line for natural, in-character delivery (and Autofit's time budget). Off: dubs use the Fast translation result.

errors.title: This tab hit a snag.
errors.desc: Don't worry — the rest of the app still works. You can switch tabs, or try again below.
errors.crash_port_in_use: The backend could not start because port 3900 is already in use — another copy of VoiceStudio (or an app that claimed that port) is holding it. Quit the other instance and relaunch; if nothing is visibly running, an orphaned backend from a previous session is still holding the port.
errors.crash_oom_kill: It was force-killed (signal 9), which usually means the operating system ran out of memory (RAM) and stopped it. Close memory-heavy apps, pick a smaller ASR model in Settings → Models, or flush the TTS model before transcribing.
errors.crash_native_fault: It crashed inside the compute stack rather than running out of memory — that points at a GPU driver that does not match the bundled CUDA runtime, or a model file that downloaded incompletely. Update your GPU driver, then re-download the model from Settings → Models (it repairs a partial download in place). If it keeps happening, switch to a crash-isolated engine in Settings → Engines — "VoiceStudio (subprocess)" for synthesis, "Faster-Whisper (crash-isolated subprocess)" for transcription. Those run the model in a separate process, so a crash like this takes down that process instead of the whole backend.
errors.report_failed: Couldn't open the bug report. Please try again, or copy the details above into a new issue.
errors.backend_shutting_down: VoiceStudio is shutting down. Reopen the app and try again.
errors.crash_broken_env: It died while loading its own Python dependencies, so this is not about memory or your GPU — the environment is incomplete or was left half-updated. Use "Clean & Retry" in Settings → Logs → Backend, which rebuilds it from scratch; that repairs it in place, without touching your voices or projects. If it still fails afterwards, the crash details name the exact package that would not import.
errors.crash_vram_default: On smaller GPUs the usual cause is running out of VRAM while loading the ASR model on top of the TTS model: flush the TTS model first, or pick a smaller ASR model in the engine's Weights list in Model Catalogue.
errors.stream_cut_backend_alive: Check the reverse proxy or load balancer in front of the app first: turn off response buffering for this route (proxy_buffering off; X-Accel-Buffering: no) and raise its read timeout. The connection was cut while the backend stayed up, so nothing crashed; a proxy on a served or containerised install is the usual cause, and running the desktop app directly or on localhost would rule it in or out.
errors.stream_cut_backend_alive_local: Wait a few minutes, then reopen the job from its history; if it is not there, read the backend log under Settings → Logs → Backend. The connection dropped mid-job after a long quiet step, but the backend is still running and normally completes the work, so this was not a crash.

crash.notice: The voice backend crashed ({{exit}}) {{ago}} ago and is being restarted automatically.
crash.details_intro: The backend process died unexpectedly ({{exit}}) {{ago}} ago. The error output it left behind is below — reporting it helps us fix the crash.
crash.notice_unclean: The previous session ended without a clean shutdown {{ago}} ago. This is often harmless — the machine slept, the app was force-quit, or a VM/container stopped.
crash.details_intro_unclean: The previous run's shutdown marker was never cleared, {{ago}} ago. VoiceStudio cannot tell whether it crashed or was simply interrupted — sleeping, force-quitting, or stopping a VM/container leaves the same trace. If everything works now, nothing needs doing.
crash.report_needs_log: No error output was captured for this event, so a one-click report would be empty. If something is actually wrong, please attach the last lines of Settings → Logs → Backend to a new issue.

backend_start_failure.notice: VoiceStudio's backend couldn't start — nothing can run until it does.
backend_start_failure.title: The backend couldn't start
backend_start_failure.intro: The app captured this while trying to start the backend. Including this output in a report helps us fix it.
backend_start_failure.retry_hint: Try "Retry" in Settings → Logs → Backend. If it fails again, "Clean & Retry" rebuilds the environment from scratch.

backendUnreachable.contact_recent: It was answering {{ago}} ago and then stopped responding, and no crash was recorded — so it may still be alive but wedged on a heavy job that is holding the engine.
backendUnreachable.contact_never: It has not answered at all this session — it may never have started.
backendUnreachable.dev: Can't reach the local VoiceStudio backend. {{contact}} In `bun run dev` the backend runs with auto-reload, so any file change — including a save while a request was in flight — restarts it and drops the connection. Retry the action first; if it was a reload, it just works. If it keeps failing, check the terminal running `bun run dev` for a Python traceback or an exit banner, and omnivoice.log in your VoiceStudio data folder for the last thing the backend logged.
backendUnreachable.server: Can't reach the VoiceStudio backend server. {{contact}} Check the server logs for the cause (e.g. `docker logs <container>` or `journalctl`) — and note that if Docker serves this page, the page itself can go down with the backend.
backendUnreachable.misrouted: The server answering {{url}} is not a VoiceStudio backend — it returned its own 404 page. API requests are landing on the wrong host: check the Backend URL in Settings → Sharing, or, if a reverse proxy serves this UI, its route for API paths.
